programs.name: Bachelor of Advanced Computing (Honours)
programs.a_level_offer: ANU selection rank 85 = GCE A-level aggregate of 14 from the best 3 subjects or 16 from the best 4 (A*=6, A=5, B=4, C=3, D=2, E=1). All A-levels must be taken in the same academic year, except one subject, which may be from the preceding or following year.
programs.ib_offer: 33 IB points (indicative score for selection rank 85, applications for Semester 1 2027). Program prerequisite: IB Mathematics: Applications and Interpretations HL, or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL or HL.
programs.ap_offer: US high school diploma with SAT 1210 (selection rank 85; SAT is accepted alongside a US high school diploma), or with 3 to 4 AP subjects taken in the same year or across two years (only scores of 3, 4 or 5 count): rank 85 needs an AP aggregate of 11 from 3 subjects, or 15 from 4 subjects. AP results must be sent by the College Board to ANU. The page lists no AP-specific subject prerequisite; the program prerequisite is stated only as IB or Australian Mathematics subjects (see required subjects).
programs.required_subjects: Mathematics. For the IB: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretations HL, or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL or HL. The page gives no A-level or AP equivalent of this prerequisite.
programs.toefl_note: TOEFL iBT (0-120 scale, TOEFL iBT Australia only for tests taken from 21 Jan 2026): for study starting on or after 1 Jan 2027, overall 81 with reading 16, writing 19, listening 16, speaking 19. The ANU policy gives no score on the new 1-6 scale.
programs.english_note: ANU undergraduate English language requirements, Table 2 of the ANU English language admission policy (ANUP_000408). Also accepted: PTE Academic 64 (60 in each skill) and Cambridge C1 Advanced 169 for study starting on or after 1 Jan 2027.
programs.notes: Selection rank 85 is the rank at which admission is guaranteed (subject to prerequisites); the minimum unadjusted rank to be considered is 70 and ANU says competitive ranking may be adjusted for applicants from across the world. The same page lists ATAR 85 and IB 33. Students completing the IB Diploma, an Australian Year 12 or the NCEA apply through UAC International; A-level and US-curriculum applicants apply directly to ANU (https://study.anu.edu.au/apply/international-applications). Semester 1 2027 international applications close 15 December 2026. Fee: the page lists an annual indicative international fee of A$57,640 for 2027, based on 48 units a year (fees vary by course choice and rise each year). The page names the Bachelor of Computing as a pathway into this degree. Conversion tables used above: A-levels https://study.anu.edu.au/apply/international-applications/indicative-entry-requirement/gce-levels ; IB (applications for Semester 1 2027) https://study.anu.edu.au/apply/undergraduate-program-indicative-entry-requirements/international-baccalaureate-applications ; SAT https://study.anu.edu.au/apply/undergraduate-program-indicative-entry-requirements/usa-scholastic-aptitude-test-sat ; AP https://study.anu.edu.au/apply/international-applications/indicative-entry-requirement/advanced-placement-ap-applications (this AP table is labelled for applications effective from Semester 1, 2026; no 2027 AP page was found).
